issues.location: Knowledge Wiki/wiki/Cross-Entropy from NLL.md:24 (table row `| **Olah / this lesson (P1 L09)** | Q | P | H(P,Q) ≥ **H(Q)** |`, reinforced by line 90 `+ P1 L09 (Information Theory: H(P,Q), floor, conventions)`)
issues.issue: The page attributes the Olah letter convention (weights from Q, floor H(Q)) to "P1 L09", but the fetched source P1 L09 (phases/01-math-foundations/09-information-theory/docs/en.md) uses the OPPOSITE convention, the one the page itself lists under "Rohit + most ML code and texts": source line 71 `H(P, Q) = -sum( p(x) * log(q(x)) )  for all x`, line 74 `P is the true distribution (the labels). Q is your model's predictions.`, and line 90 `= H(P, Q) - H(P)`. So "P1 L09" appears in the Olah/KL-floor row (line 24), in the header as Rohit's lesson (line 3/5: `Rohit P1 L09, Checkpoint 3`, `Source: Rohit P1 L06 + P1 L09 + Olah`), and again in the Source section credited with `H(P,Q), floor, conventions` (line 90) — the same identifier is claimed for both conventions. The deliberate deviation is a property of THIS lesson (the lesson_ref states `this lesson uses Olah-style H(P,Q) ... Rohit/ML convention flips the letters`), not of Rohit's P1 L09 en.md. As written, a learner who re-reads the cited source while applying the page's own advice (line 29, `Check which letter carries the data before grading a formula`) will conclude the page contradicts its primary source. Fix: label the row `Olah (and this lesson)` and only credit P1 L09 with the flipped-letters convention, stating the deviation explicitly.

issues.location: Knowledge Wiki/wiki/Cross-Entropy from NLL.md:29 — `So the statement "H(P,Q) ≥ H(P)" is true under the Rohit/ML convention (P = truth) and false under this lesson's convention (P = model).`
issues.issue: The sentence asserts a truth value the page's own worked numbers contradict under the lesson's letters: with truth Q = (0.75,0.25) and model P = (0.5,0.5), H(P,Q) = 1.0 and H(P) = 1.0, i.e. H(P,Q) ≥ H(P) holds with equality; with the E3 coin Q = (0.9,0.1), P = (0.25,0.75), H(P,Q) = 1.84 ≥ H(P) ≈ 0.81 also holds. What is actually false under the lesson's convention is the general FLOOR CLAIM (a counterexample exists: weights q = (0.99,0.01), surprises p = (0.9,0.1) gives 0.184 < 0.469). Since the learner's tracked misconception (Core/🧯 Mistakes.md, 2026-09-12 row) is precisely "the floor is the model's entropy H(P)", the flat "false" next to an example where the inequality visibly holds is a re-anchoring hazard. Fix: say it "is not a valid floor rule here — the floor is H(Q)" instead of "false".

The envelope URL 404s (repo slug is `ai-engineering-from-scratch`, not `ai-engineer-from-scratch`). Review was therefore done against the corrected URL for the same lesson (HTTP 200, 471 lines, cited by Learning System/CURRICULUM.md:61 `phases/01-math-foundations/09-* ... docs/en.md`). No wiki-content change needed; the typo is bookkeeping/traceability only.
